sources: Ellen MacArthur Foundation single-use plastics data (disposal estimates)
_meta.note: Synthetic baseline. 5 lifecycle phases. Phase 4 (Disposal) is the critical bottleneck at 62.0% balance.

0.name: Resource Definition & Material Sourcing
0.notes: Raw material feedstocks are globally traded commodities with published spot prices. Butane: NYMEX C4; PP resin: ICIS Polyolefins. China is net LPG importer. Key risk: geopolitical supply concentration in Middle East and Russia for butane feedstock.

1.name: Manufacturing & Assembly
1.notes: 3,000 Wenzhou manufacturers operating on sub-cent margins per unit. ISO 9994 tolerance constraints (D) are extreme; contribution (C) is fragmented across many small private actors. Injection molding energy intensity is high but not tracked at unit level. No renewable energy transition underway in Wenzhou lighter cluster.

2.name: Distribution & Retail
2.notes: Global reach to 150+ countries. Certification requirements (ISO 9994; EN 13869; CPSC) act as D-constraints enabling market access. BIC brand premium ($0.60/unit) is the primary E-layer finding: the only abstract value decoupling in the entire supply chain.

3.name: Use Phase
3.notes: High D-C balance: the lighter performs reliably within ISO 9994 bounds. Approximately 3,000 ignitions per unit. Average useful life 2-12 weeks depending on usage frequency. Single-use design: no refill pathway for non-refillable variants. Product engineered for disposability, not for lifecycle.

4.name: Disposal & Circularity
4.notes: LIFECYCLE BOTTLENECK. Near-zero recycling rate: >99% of 10 billion annual units go to landfill. PP body (5g per unit = 50,000 MT PP/year) is technically recyclable but not collected. Residual butane makes the product hazardous waste if not fully exhausted. No manufacturer take-back program at scale. Butane venting: approximately 40,000 MT/year from incompletely exhausted units. The lighter is the canonical example of a commodity optimized for production cost at the complete expense of lifecycle circularity.

system.sustainability_finding: The lighter lifecycle is characterized by high operational efficiency (Phases 0-3 all above 70% balance) and catastrophic end-of-life failure (Phase 4 at 62.0% balance; sustainability index 0.05). This is a designed feature, not an oversight: the micro-margin manufacturing model requires single-use disposability to maintain the product's price point. The true environmental cost (50,000 MT PP plastic waste/year; 40,000 MT butane venting/year) is not internalized in the $0.15 factory gate price.
system.tholonic_interpretation: The lifecycle D-C imbalance at Phase 4 (D=220 vs C=190) reveals a structural breakdown: regulatory constraints classify the lighter as hazardous waste at end of life (high D), while the contribution pathways for circularity are near-zero (low C). The parent N for the disposal phase (the physical lighter) cannot transition cleanly to a child N (a recycled material) because no tholonic boundary has been established between use and recovery. This is the tholonic signature of a closed-loop failure.
